resources.string: Korean chess
Korean chess (janggi). Tap one of your blue pieces, then a green dot. Inside the palaces pieces may also follow the diagonal lines. You may pass instead of moving. Trap the red general to win.
Your turn: tap one of your blue pieces
Tap a green dot to move there
Check! Your general is attacked: protect it
Pieces
How the pieces move

Pieces stand on the line crossings. On each piece, a dot is one step, two dots mark the longer jump of the elephant, an arrow means any distance, an arrow with a bar means it must jump over one piece, and a hollow dot is a diagonal step allowed only along the lines of a palace.
General (楚, 漢): one step along the lines of the palace, diagonals included. It never leaves the palace.
Guard (士): moves like the general, one step along the palace lines, and stays in the palace.
Elephant (象): one point straight, then two diagonally outward. Blocked if a point on the way is taken.
Horse (馬): one point straight, then one diagonally outward. Blocked if the first point is taken.
Chariot (車): any distance along a line, and along the diagonal lines inside a palace.
Cannon (包): must jump over exactly one piece to move or to capture. It never jumps over or captures another cannon.
Soldier (卒, 兵): one step forward or sideways, never back. Inside the enemy palace it may also step diagonally forward along the lines.
